themes_detail.label: Street noise surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 43 THIS WEEK, a 421% increase from the 8.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.7), suggesting a sudden, acute disruption affecting multiple blocks in St. George/Stapleton.
evidence: 43 noise-street/sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.2 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Z-score of 6.7 indicates statistically significant spike
421% increase from baseline suggests sudden onset, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Knock on doors in high-complaint blocks this week; identify common source (construction, venue, event, traffic pattern change)
Check DOT and FDNY permit databases for new street work, entertainment licenses, or events filed in past 7-10 days

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66), indicating a sudden enforcement action, illegal vending cluster, or new complaint awareness in the district.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Z-score of 8.66 indicates statistically significant anomaly
May signal either complaint surge or coordinated enforcement push
reporting_angles: DCVB and SLA records: Was a new enforcement push launched this week? Any street vending violations or license suspensions filed?
Interview street vendors on high-complaint corners about police/city interaction patterns in the past 7 days

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 5 LAST WEEK from a near-zero baseline of 0.2 weekly average (1900% increase, z-score: 10.97—the district's highest statistical anomaly), indicating a major event, new usage pattern, or maintenance activity at a major park.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Z-score of 10.97—the single highest statistical anomaly across all complaint categories
Liotti Ikefugi Playground Reconstruction is in active public review (milestone: post-hearing follow-up)
reporting_angles: Check Parks Dept. event permits and Liotti Ikefugi Playground reconstruction timeline; confirm whether noise is construction-related or event-driven
Visit the park; document noise sources and survey residents on frequency, duration, and impact on quality of life

themes_detail.label: Safety complaints spike 2 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints jumped to 27 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 6.9 weekly average (293% increase, z-score: 5.67), indicating a cluster of security incidents or public disorder that may have since resolved or evolved into other complaint categories.
evidence: 27 safety complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 6.9 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Z-score of 5.67 indicates statistically significant spike
Timeframe suggests incident(s) occurred; current status unclear from 311 data alone
reporting_angles: NYPD crime data: Were there arrests, robbery, assault, or gang-related incidents in the district 10-14 days ago?
Community board meeting minutes or Nextdoor posts: What safety issues have residents flagged in the past 2-3 weeks?

themes_detail.label: Drug activity complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints rose to 5 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.8 weekly average (567% increase, z-score: 5.13), pointing to either a localized open-air drug market, visible use, or trafficking cluster in one or more blocks.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Converges with safety spike from 2 weeks ago; may indicate ongoing public order deterioration
reporting_angles: NYPD arrest data: Drug arrests or summons in the district last 7-10 days; identify block clusters
Canvass affected blocks; speak with residents, local business owners, and outreach workers about visible drug use or trafficking locations
